To find $V_{Th}$,

Applying node voltage method,

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
\left(\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{2}\right) & -\frac{1}{6} & -\frac{1}{6} \\
-\frac{1}{6} & \left(\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}\right) & -\frac{1}{6} \\
-\frac{1}{6} & -\frac{1}{6} & \left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}\right)
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}
V_A \\
V_B \\
V_C
\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
6 \\
6 \\
0
\end{bmatrix}
$$

Solving we get, $V_B = V_{Th} = 30\,\text{V}$

To find $R_{Th}$

$\Rightarrow R_{Th} = 4\,\Omega$

$$
P_{\max} = \frac{V_{Th}^2}{4R_{Th}} = 56.25\,\text{W}
$$

Voltage leading the current by $45^\circ$ $\Rightarrow \angle Z = 45^\circ$

Total impedance $= Z = R + (jX_L \parallel -jX_C) = R + j\dfrac{X_LX_C}{X_L-X_C}$

$$
45 = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{X_LX_C}{R(X_L-X_C)}\right) \Rightarrow X_C = 8.5714\,\Omega
$$

$\therefore C = 116.66\,\mu\text{F}$

diagrams.caption: Power triangle showing P = 5000 W with old and new reactive powers. (original source region)

questions.markdown:
From the power triangle,

$$
\tan(\phi_{\text{old}})=\frac{Q_{\text{old}}}{P} \Rightarrow Q_{\text{old}} = 3750\,\text{var}
$$

Similarly,

$$
\tan(\phi_{\text{new}})=\frac{Q_{\text{new}}}{P} \Rightarrow Q_{\text{new}} = 2421.61\,\text{var}
$$

$\therefore Q_c = Q_{\text{old}} - Q_{\text{new}} \Rightarrow Q_c = 1328.38\,\text{var}$

$$
Q_c = \frac{V^2}{X_c} \Rightarrow X_c = 36.43\,\Omega \Rightarrow C = 87.36\,\mu\text{F}
$$

Given, $\bar{V}_L = 400\angle 0^\circ\,\text{V} \Rightarrow \bar{V}_{ph} = 230.94\angle -30^\circ\,\text{V}$

$$
\hat{Z} = \frac{230.94\angle -30^\circ}{10\angle -66.86^\circ} \Rightarrow \hat{Z} = 23.09\angle 36.86^\circ\,\Omega
$$

$\therefore R = |Z|\cos\theta = 18.474\,\Omega$

$X_L = |Z|\sin\theta = 13.85\,\Omega \Rightarrow L = 44.08\,\text{mH}$

Power factor $= \cos\theta = 0.8$ lagging

$P = 3V_{ph}I_{ph}\cos\theta = 5542.56\,\text{W}$

$Q = 3V_{ph}I_{ph}\sin\theta = 4155.96\,\text{var}$

$S = 3V_{ph}I_{ph} = 6928.2\,\text{VA}$
